newsitem.title: FRANCE: Versailles bans controversial "Larry Flynt" poster.
newsitem.headline: Versailles bans controversial "Larry Flynt" poster.

text.p: The mayor of Versailles has asked that posters for the Hollywood film "The People vs Larry Flynt" be taken down ahead of a court ruling.
Two Paris judges are to rule on Thursday on calls for a nationwide ban on the posters for the film, about pornography and censorship.

"This poster deeply offends the feelings of believers," Etienne Pinte, mayor of Versailles west of Paris told Europe 1 radio on Wednesday. "That's the reason I've asked for this poster to be withdrawn."
The town, site of Louis XIV's palace, is a stronghold of traditional Catholic belief.

The posters show actor Woody Harrelson, arms outstretched in a position recalling that of Jesus Christ on the cross, wearing only an American flag around his hips against a backdrop of a woman's bikini-clad pelvis.
The film, which won two Academy Award nominations in Los Angeles last week, focuses on the trial of U.S. hard-core pornography publisher Larry Flynt, founder of "Hustler" magazine.
"The assimilation of Christ to a 'crucified' pornographer is intolerable," Louis-Marie Bille, president of the French Bishops' Conference, said in a statement, calling it "dishonest and aberrant".

He said the issues raised by the poster were not restricted to Catholics. "The freedom of everyone...is in question," he wrote, saying that xenophobia could gain ground when society dropped respect for different groups.
The film's producer Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp, argue the posters are protected by freedom of expression.
